dedupe_keys.name: vehicle inventory and use survey vius

description: The Vehicle Inventory and Use Survey (VIUS) is conducted by the U.S. Census Bureau and sponsored by the Bureau of Transportation Statistics, the Federal Highway Administration and the Department of Energy to describe the physical and operational characteristics of the nation's truck population. Its universe is all private and commercial trucks registered in the United States: pickups, minivans and other light vans, sport utility vehicles, light and heavy single-unit trucks and truck-tractors; it excludes vehicles owned by federal, state and local governments, among others. With a sample of 150,000 vehicles it estimates truck counts and miles by body type, weight, fuel, age, operating range, cargo carried, business use and other characteristics, at national and state level. Coverage: the 2021 survey, the first since 2002; its predecessor, the Truck Inventory and Use Survey, ran with the Census of Transportation from 1963 to 2002. 2021 tables were released on 28 September 2023, with an experimental product adding model-based estimates for New Hampshire, which did not take part. Access: data tables, a Public Use File on the Microdata Access Tool, and the Census Data API (viusa to viusf and viuspuf); free and public domain. Caveats: long gaps between editions, New Hampshire modelled, and no vehicle locations or trips. Simulation uses: truck fleet composition, payload and mileage for freight transport, emissions and electrification models, pavement loading and fuel demand scenarios. Related records: Commodity Flow Survey, Freight Analysis Framework and BTS freight indicators.
